name: Gynecomastia compression vest

card.summary: A tight vest that hides male chest tissue under clothes; it conceals gynecomastia but no studies test it.
card.note: Concealment only; persistent or painful breast enlargement is a medical question.

lead: A gynecomastia compression vest is a snug, stretchy undershirt or vest worn by men to press the chest flatter so that enlarged male breast tissue shows less through a T-shirt or dress shirt. Wearers use it to get a smoother, more masculine-looking chest outline in everyday clothing, at the gym or at the beach under a rash guard, without waiting for or undergoing treatment. It changes the outline over the tissue rather than the tissue itself. [1][2]

Gynecomastia is the benign enlargement of male breast tissue. Wikipedia reports that it affects about 35 percent of men at some point and that up to 70 percent of adolescent boys develop it to some degree, with roughly 75 percent of those teenage cases resolving within two years without treatment. [1] Wikipedia notes that the condition is associated with self-consciousness and body-image concerns, particularly in adolescents. [1]

Wikipedia's article on compression garments includes a short entry on the gynecomastia vest, describing it as a specialised garment for men with the condition and as a non-surgical option for those who choose to compress the breast. [2] No published trial has tested compression vests for gynecomastia; research on compression vests concerns other conditions. [3][4]

angle.text: The vest changes how the chest reads under clothing the moment it is put on, and it comes off at the end of the day. Wearers use it for a flatter outline while puberty-related enlargement runs its course, or while they decide whether to pursue medical or surgical options.

paras: Gynecomastia arises from an imbalance between estrogen and androgen activity at the breast. Listed causes include puberty, ageing, obesity, medications and substances such as anabolic steroids and spironolactone, chronic illness and low testosterone, and in about a quarter of cases no cause is found. [1]

Wikipedia notes that, although physically benign, the condition is associated with distress, body-image concerns and social withdrawal, particularly among adolescents, and that research on these effects is more limited than research on causes and treatment. [1] Treatment is generally considered when it persists beyond two years or causes pain or embarrassment. Medical options include tamoxifen, which is not FDA-approved for the purpose, and surgery is described as the most effective known treatment for persistent cases. [1]

Vests are elastic compression garments, often a nylon or spandex blend, worn against the skin like an undershirt. They are sold in sleeveless, short-sleeve and zip-front styles and are marketed for hiding gynecomastia under shirts, including while puberty-related cases resolve or before surgery. [2] Wikipedia's compression-garment article places them alongside other medical and sport compression wear, which are worn to provide support, manage swelling or reduce chafing. [2]

Sizing matters to how the garment performs: a vest that is too loose does not flatten the chest, and one that is too tight can feel restrictive. This reflects how such products are generally described by sellers rather than a finding from published research.

Surgery for gynecomastia includes subcutaneous mastectomy, liposuction-assisted mastectomy and laser-assisted liposuction. Reported complications include hematoma, infection, asymmetry, seroma and scarring. [1] Liposuction for gynecomastia has been described in the plastic-surgery literature since at least 1987. [5]

Wikipedia reports that 24,123 men had gynecomastia surgery in the United States in 2019 and that many insurers classify it as cosmetic. [1] Some men wear a vest as a non-surgical alternative or to bridge the time before a procedure. [2]

No studies found of compression vests for gynecomastia. Compression vests have been studied in other settings: a pilot study of 25 women with breast or chest-wall edema after breast cancer treatment reported on pain scores while wearing a compression vest, and a randomized trial of 242 patients compared a compression vest with a pressure cuff to a sandbag for pocket hematoma after cardiac device implantation. These studies do not address gynecomastia or appearance. [3][4]

quick.overview:
A gynecomastia compression vest is an elastic undershirt that flattens the chest so enlarged male breast tissue shows less through clothing. It does not change the tissue underneath.

Gynecomastia is common in adolescence, and most teenage cases resolve within about two years. No studies were found that test compression garments for it.
quick.mechanism: Pressure from the elastic fabric holds the chest tissue flatter against the body, which changes the outline under a shirt.
quick.risks: No published safety data for these vests were found. Medical sources describe observation, medication and surgery as the management routes for persistent gynecomastia, and note that some causes, such as drugs or illness, are evaluated by clinicians.
